title: Brahmam Okkate
translator: Claude (Opus 5.5) in Claude Code, using the Svara skill. Draft for a human lyricist to review.

lines.meaning: Tandanana, ahi, tandanana, pure (sung vocables with no dictionary meaning)
lines.notes: Vocables are kept as sung. Translating them would lose the folk rhythm the whole song rests on.
"Bhala" is a cheer ("well done"), so it stays as a sound, the way "hey" would in English.

lines.meaning: Brahman (the ultimate reality) is one; the supreme Brahman is one.
lines.singable: The Truth is only one, the Highest Truth is one

lines.meaning: The supreme Brahman is one, the supreme Brahman is one.
lines.singable: Oh, the Highest Truth is one, yes, the Highest Truth is one
lines.notes: "Is one" ends every okkate / okate line, so the English keeps one end rhyme the whole way through, as the Telugu does.

lines.meaning: Here there is no such thing as lower and higher.
lines.singable: Here there is no high, there is no low, no rank at all

lines.meaning: For everyone, Sri Hari is the soul within.
lines.singable: In all of us, Hari is the inner soul

lines.meaning: In this, all the kinds of living creatures are one.
lines.singable: Every living creature here, all of them are one

lines.meaning: For everyone, Sri Hari is the soul within.
lines.singable: In all of us, Hari is the inner soul

lines.meaning: The sleep a king sleeps in full comfort,
lines.singable: The sleep a king sleeps on his soft and silken bed

lines.meaning: and the sleep of the servant beside him: that too is one and the same.
lines.singable: And the servant's sleep beside him, that sleep too is one

lines.meaning: The earth a lofty Brahmin steps on is one,
lines.singable: The very ground the high-born Brahmin walks on is one

lines.meaning: and the earth where the outcast lives is the same one.
lines.singable: And the ground where the outcast lives is that same one
lines.notes: The original names the caste (chandala). "Outcast" keeps the point of the verse, that the highest and the lowest stand on the same earth, without the slur.

notes: Hari (Vishnu) is kept by name rather than translated to "God": the kirtana is addressed to him, and the name is two syllables that land on two notes.
